Fifteenth Finance Commission award begins and Jammu and Kashmir leaves the denominator of the states' share; the pool itself also reaches its trough at 74.0 per cent.
Reporting-base shift stated by the Commission itself: actual CAG certificate through FY2023-24, Union Budget Revised and Budget Estimates thereafter.

points.note: The last year before the FC-XIV award took effect, and the figure FC-XVI itself uses as its benchmark at para 7.67.
The trough of the published series.

Independently reproduced at T1: CAG-certified net proceeds 27,69,957.40 crore against gross tax revenue 34,65,519 crore (Receipt Budget 2026-27, Annex 4C and Annex 1) = 79.93 per cent. The two documents agree to the second decimal. Last year on a certified basis.
Revised Estimate basis, not a certificate.
Budget Estimate basis, not a certificate.

notes: This is the arithmetic bridge between "the states get 41 per cent" and "the states get about 32 per cent of gross tax revenue": roughly a fifth to a quarter of gross tax revenue sits outside the pool the 41 per cent is applied to. Award-period means stated by FC-XVI at para 7.35 and used as a reconciliation control: FC-XIII 89.2, FC-XIV 82.16, FC-XV 78.32; all three reconcile from the annual values above. The control is necessary because pdftotext scrambles bar-chart label order, and it is what fixes the year-to-value assignment. caveat: Read this against fc-vertical-devolution-share, never alone. A rising share of central taxes applied to a shrinking pool is the whole substance of the phase's fiscal argument, and either series read on its own supports the opposite conclusion from the pair.

title: Cesses and surcharges as a share of gross tax revenue, GST Compensation Cess included
unit: per cent of Union gross tax revenue

source.name: Fifteenth Finance Commission, Report for 2021-26, Volume I — Main Report, Table 3.8 "Cesses and Surcharges" (p. 67). The Commission states its source as "Union Budget documents".

breaks.note: The GST Compensation Cess enters the aggregate. It is a levy earmarked to the states, and including it in a measure of what the Union keeps out of the pool inverts the finding — the excl-comp-cess series falls in this year while this one rises.

The direct-tax component jumps 2.7-fold, from 53,433 to 1,45,802 crore: the 4 per cent Health and Education Cess replacing the 3 per cent Education Cess, plus a reclassification under which the same money is counted as both a cess and a surcharge.

Reporting basis changes: Actual through FY2018-19, Revised Estimate FY2019-20, Budget Estimate FY2020-21. The last two rows do not reconcile against outturn gross tax revenue and are not measurements of the same kind as the first eight.

points.note: Reproduced from the Commission's own rupee figures: 2,66,574 / 19,19,008 = 13.89 per cent.
Revised Estimate. Does not reconcile against outturn gross tax revenue — the same rupee figure over actual GTR gives 21.7 per cent — which is the expected behaviour of an estimate row.
Budget Estimate.

notes: This is the phase's central number in its most-cited form and the doubling is real on this convention: 10.4 per cent of gross tax revenue in FY2011-12 to 19.9-20.2 per cent by FY2018-19. Roughly a quarter of the end-period level is the GST Compensation Cess, which is earmarked to the states.
caveat: Never quote this series without naming its convention. The same quantity for FY2024-25 has four defensible values spanning 9.98 to 17.71 per cent depending on whether the GST Compensation Cess and the Special Additional Excise Duty are counted — a spread larger than the entire rise this series is used to demonstrate.

title: Cesses and surcharges as a share of gross tax revenue, GST Compensation Cess excluded
unit: per cent of Union gross tax revenue

source.name: Derived from Fifteenth Finance Commission, Volume I — Main Report, Table 3.8 (p. 67), by subtracting the Commission's own broken-out GST Compensation Cess row from its own total row. The Commission publishes both rows so that the subtraction can be made.

breaks.note: GST begins. On this convention the share FALLS in FY2017-18, from 13.5 to 10.6, while the comp-cess-inclusive series RISES from 13.5 to 13.9. The two series move in opposite directions in the same year and it is not a rounding artefact.
Actual to Revised Estimate to Budget Estimate, as in the parent table.

points.note: Corroborated independently at T1: FC-XV para 4.25 states that cesses and surcharges excluding the compensation cess amounted to 3.18 lakh crore in FY2018-19 and averaged 13.1 per cent of GTR over FY2016-17 to FY2018-19; the mean of 13.5, 10.6 and 15.3 is 13.13.
Revised Estimate.
Budget Estimate.

notes: Excluding the compensation cess, the rise from FY2011-12 to FY2020-21 is 10.4 to 15.3 — a multiple of 1.47, against 1.91 on the inclusive convention. The GST Compensation Cess accounts for roughly half of the apparent doubling. This is a separate series from cess-surcharge-share-gtr, not a variant of it, because the choice of convention inverts the sign of the FY2017-18 movement.
caveat: This series and cess-surcharge-share-gtr must be shown together or neither. Either alone answers the question whether the Union enlarged the money it does not share in a way the other contradicts for FY2017-18.

title: Net proceeds of Union taxes certified by the Comptroller and Auditor General under Article 279(1)
unit: ₹ crore, current prices

source.name: Sixteenth Finance Commission, Volume I — Main Report, Table 7.4 row 5, sourced by the Commission to "CAG certificate" (FY2018-19 to FY2022-23); Union Receipt Budget 2026-2027, Annex 4C, "Disclosure Statement of Data on Net Proceeds as certified by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India as per Article 279 of the Constitution for FY 2023-2024" (FY2023-24).

points.note: States' entitlement at 42 per cent = 7,09,544 crore; the ratio reproduces to 42.00 per cent exactly, as it must, the entitlement row being defined as 0.42 times this one.

From Receipt Budget 2026-27 Annex 4C, the first and so far only publication of the certificate in its own right. States' share at 41 per cent = 11,35,682.53 crore against releases of 11,36,306.00 crore, giving a final settlement of minus 623.47 crore — a recovery from the states. Integrated GST and the GST Compensation Cess are both named as lines and valued at a dash: the Article 270(1) exclusion rendered as an audited number.

notes: Six years is the whole published series. Before FY2018-19 no CAG-certified pool is published in any form. Article 279(1) has required the certificate since 1950 and makes it final; it has been disclosed once, for one year, by the paying party, and only because the Sixteenth Finance Commission recommended the disclosure in 2025.
caveat: No Article 279(1) certificate has ever been published as a document of the Comptroller and Auditor General. Every point here is the certified figure as relayed by a party to the dispute — five by the Commission the Union appoints, one by the Union's own Receipt Budget. The Regulations on Audit and Accounts 2020 contain no occurrence of "net proceeds", "proceeds" or "279", so no regulation governs the certificate at all.

title: States' share of the divisible pool of central taxes recommended by the Finance Commission
unit: per cent of the divisible pool of central taxes

source.name: Sixteenth Finance Commission, Volume I — Main Report, para 7.68 and paras 7.8-7.16, read against each Commission's own recommendation: FC-XIII para 8.17, FC-XIV para 8.13, FC-XV paras 6.9 and 6.29.

denominator: the divisible pool of central taxes — gross tax revenue less cesses, surcharges, Union Territory taxes and cost of collection

breaks.note: FC-XIV, 32 to 42 per cent. The largest single-step increase in the institution's history and a real increase. FC-XIV para 8.13 gives four reasons, the first of which is "States not being entitled to the growing share of cess and surcharges in the revenues of the Union Government".

FC-XV, 42 to 41 per cent. NOT a cut: FC-XV para 6.9 says the Commission "only adjusted for the newly carved out Union Territories of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh, keeping the balance share broadly equivalent at 41 per cent for the remaining twenty-eight States". FC-XVI para 7.16 puts the adjustment at approximately 1 per cent of the divisible pool.
FC-XVI award begins. The value does not change, but the award, the horizontal formula and the entire grant architecture do, so every series keyed to an award breaks here even though this one is flat.

points.note: FC-XIII para 8.17: "we recommend that the share of states in the net proceeds of shareable central taxes be raised from 30.5 per cent to 32 per cent".
FC-XV first (one-year) report.
FC-XV final report, para 6.29.

FC-XVI para 7.68, accepted by the Union in the Explanatory Memorandum of 1 February 2026. The Commission's stated reason is the pool itself: "With cesses and surcharges having cut the size of the divisible pool from 89.1 per cent of GTR in 2014-15 to a 74-80 per cent range... there is no room for cutting the States' share in it."

notes: A step function by award, carried annually because the share applies to each year's proceeds. The number is a recommendation the Union accepted in each case; it is not a measure of what was paid. For what was paid, read fc-devolution-share-of-gtr and devolution-be-to-actual-gap. This is a rule and not a measurement, which is why multiplying it by divisible-pool-share-gtr does not reproduce fc-devolution-share-of-gtr in any year — see P-116.

FC-XV award begins and Jammu and Kashmir leaves the states' denominator.

points.note: FC-XIII award average is 27.9.

NOT the high-water mark of devolution. Devolution went out against a Revised Estimate gross tax revenue of 22,48,175 crore; actuals came in 1,67,710 crore short after the cash had moved. FC-XVI Table 7.4 records the first retrospective adjustment for FY2018-19 as minus 58,843 crore, a clawback.
FC-XIV award average is 34.0.
Last year on an Actuals basis. Table 7.5 continues to FY2024-25 (33.9, Revised Estimate) and FY2025-26 (33.3, Budget Estimate); those two rows are deliberately not carried here.

notes: The series stops at FY2023-24 because the Commission's own FC-XV award average of 32.1 splices Actuals, a Revised Estimate and a Budget Estimate in one mean and does not flag it. Part 02 recomputed every row of Table 7.5 from the rupee figures in Annexure 7.1: all sixteen devolution rows and all sixteen grant rows reproduce to the published decimal, which confirms Table 7.5 is a derivation of Annexure 7.1 and not an independent source. Do NOT reconstruct this series by multiplying divisible-pool-share-gtr by fc-vertical-devolution-share: the product misses in every year, by between minus 1.70 and plus 1.80 percentage points, and the sign changes six times. Two of the three are rules and this one is cash moved in the year. P-116 sets out why and prints the residuals.
caveat: This is devolution against gross tax revenue, not against the divisible pool. The gap between this series (about 32 per cent) and fc-vertical-devolution-share (41 per cent) is not underpayment; it is divisible-pool-share-gtr. Reading either number as the other is the commonest error in this subject.

That is a positive control the Commission ran and printed on gross tax revenue; it ran no such control on its devolution column.

source.name: Sixteenth Finance Commission, Volume II — Annexures, Annexure 7.1.

FC-XV award begins.

points.note: Against an entitlement of 7,09,544 crore attributed to the same year by FC-XVI Table 7.4 — a difference of plus 37,350 crore, because this column measures cash moved in the year and that one measures entitlement after retrospective adjustment.
Entitlement 6,82,675 crore; difference minus 31,988 crore.
Entitlement 6,14,978 crore; difference minus 19,751 crore.
Entitlement 8,36,460 crore; difference plus 46,640 crore.
Entitlement 9,71,005 crore; difference minus 22,023 crore.

notes: On a year-by-year cash basis, devolution ranged 39.68 to 44.21 per cent of the certified pool over FY2018-19 to FY2022-23 while the recommended share was a flat 41 or 42 per cent. A state reading its own receipts in a single year will see a number that is not 41 per cent, and will be right. This series carries the Finance Commission's Annexure 7.1 and is NOT the same instrument as devolution-actual-receipt-budget, which carries the Union's own Receipt Budget Actuals under major head 0710 and is what devolution-be-to-actual-gap is computed from. The two agree in six of eleven overlapping years and diverge in four, by 67,819.29 crore in FY2017-18, 14,560.15 in FY2018-19, 15,292 in FY2021-22 and 576.18 in FY2022-23. Those divergences are the definitional gap between instruments and are NOT errors in this series; P-117 records them and L-0182 records that FY2017-18 is far larger than the rest and unexplained.

Two tables inside one Commission report give different devolution figures for the same five years, differing by up to 46,640 crore, and both are correct on their own definition. title: Tax devolution finally accounted against tax devolution budgeted for the same year
unit: per cent of the Union's Budget Estimate for tax devolution

source.name: Union Receipt Budget, Abstract of Receipts — Budget Estimate column of year T against the Actuals column of year T+2, read across eleven editions. The current edition is linked; earlier editions sit at the parallel budget<YYYY-YYYY>/ub<YY-YY>/rec/allrec.pdf and budget<YY-YY>/doc/rec/allrec.pdf paths.

denominator: the Union's own Budget Estimate of tax devolution for that year

breaks.note: The error sign-flips here and never returns. This sits exactly on the FC-XV award boundary and must NOT be read as an award effect: it is a forecasting-regime change, post-COVID gross-tax-revenue budgeting turning conservative, with the states as the residual beneficiaries.

points.note: BE 3,82,215.94 crore; Actual 3,37,808.45 crore.
BE 8,09,133.02 crore; Actual 6,50,677.05 crore — a shortfall of 1,58,456 crore, driven by a gross-tax-revenue shortfall of 18.3 per cent against BE, not by any devolution decision.
BE 7,84,180.87 crore; Actual 5,94,996.76 crore — a shortfall of 1,89,184 crore.
BE 6,65,562.74 crore; Actual 8,98,392 crore — plus 2,32,829 crore.

notes: This is the series a state finance department actually experiences. A state budgets against the Union's Budget Estimate; in FY2019-20 and FY2020-21 it lost a fifth and a quarter of the devolution it had planned on. It is carried because it is the only measured form of the states' complaint that depends on no contested definition — both columns are the Union's own, for the same quantity, in the same document series. Both inputs are now authored as series in their own right — devolution-budget-estimate and devolution-actual-receipt-budget — and (Actual minus BE) divided by BE reproduces all eleven stated values to the stated decimal. Two method rules are pinned by that recomputation rather than assumed. In the three years with two budgets, FY2014-15, FY2019-20 and FY2024-25, the series uses the FULL budget and not the interim: substituting the interim Budget Estimate breaks all three years and none of the other eight, and for FY2019-20 it would move the stated shortfall from 19.6 to 23.0 per cent. And the Budget Estimate is the Budget at a Glance headline, which for FY2018-19 is the sum of the Receipt Budget's base devolution line and its separate actual-adjustment line. The Actual column is the Union's Receipt Budget, NOT the Finance Commission's Annexure 7.1 — the two are different instruments and differ in four of eleven years, once by 67,819 crore; see P-117.
caveat: A read-trap in the source: the Receipt Budget's Tax Revenue detail pages split devolution into "Less-States' Share" plus a separate "Less-States' share adjustment as per Actual", and the Abstract of Receipts headline is the sum. Reading the detail page alone understates BE FY2018-19 devolution by 19,680 crore; these points take the Abstract. The Receipt Budget editions were retrieved and transcribed within this run by a directed retrieval agent that recorded a URL and table caption for every row, so they are one remove from the authoring part's own reading.

denominator: the states' aggregate share of the divisible pool — 29 states under FC-XIV including Jammu and Kashmir, 28 states from FC-XV

Tamil Nadu's FC-XIV award is two shares, not one — 4.023 per cent on the pool excluding service tax and 4.104 per cent on shareable service tax.
FC-XV's one-year report for FY2020-21 carries a DIFFERENT inter-se share from its final report. An award-level series is simply wrong for this year.
FC-XV final report. Jammu and Kashmir has left the 28-state denominator, so a state's number can move because the denominator moved.

FC-XVI award. Its para 8.62: "even if we were to retain the exact same criteria and associated weights as the FC-15, the States' shares shift significantly due to the updation of underlying data." Formula effect and data effect are not separable and the Commission says so.

points.note: FC-XIII. FC-XVI's Table 8.4 rounds this to 4.97.
Excluding service tax; the parallel shareable-service-tax share is 4.104 per cent.

FC-XV's first report, for FY2020-21 alone. This value is not in FC-XVI's compilation and is not the 4.079 the award is usually quoted at; it is read from the CAG's Tamil Nadu State Finances Audit Report FY2023-24, Table 2.7. FC-XVI Table 8.9, accepted by the Union on 1 February 2026. Tamil Nadu's share rises slightly under the new formula.

The FC-XI and FC-XII values, 5.39 and 5.31, exist only at two decimals in FC-XVI's compilation and are outside this window.

title: Tamil Nadu's share in devolution divided by its share in population
unit: ratio of share in devolution to share in population (dimensionless; 1.00 = devolution exactly proportionate to population)

source.name: Sixteenth Finance Commission, Volume I — Main Report, Table 8.5, "Ratios of Share in Devolution to Share in Population: Non-NEH States", derived by the Commission from its own Table 8.4.

denominator: the state's share of the 2011 Census population

breaks.note: FC-XIV. The fall from 0.82 to 0.66 is minus 19.5 per cent, and excluding Andhra Pradesh — whose 1.67 to 1.04 fall is the 2014 bifurcation, not a formula effect — it is the largest fall of any non-NEH state at this step. A figure of 24 per cent circulates for this fall and is wrong.
FC-XV, recalculated by the Commission excluding Jammu and Kashmir.

points.note: No FC-XVI value exists: Table 8.5 stops at FC-XV and the Commission did not compute the ratio for its own award.

notes: Tamil Nadu at 0.66-0.67 is not an outlier among comparable states: Haryana 0.51, Maharashtra 0.58-0.67, Gujarat 0.61-0.69, Kerala 0.69, Karnataka 0.71, and the average for the eight high-per-capita-GSDP states is 0.70 under FC-XIV and 0.68 under FC-XV. Tamil Nadu sits within a hair of its group mean. FC-XVI para 8.68 records that Tamil Nadu's relative per capita share "remained virtually unchanged" under FC-XV while Telangana, Karnataka and Kerala fell sharply.
caveat: A ratio below 1.00 is not evidence of a defect. The formula is designed to devolve more per head to states with lower per capita GSDP, and FC-XVI states that each of the last five Commissions disbursed 75 per cent or more of the states' pool on equity criteria. This series measures whether the design is operating, not whether it is right.

title: West Bengal's share in devolution divided by its share in population

source.name: Sixteenth Finance Commission, Volume I — Main Report, Table 8.5.

breaks.note: FC-XIV.

notes: This is the comparator that isolates the horizontal formula. West Bengal receives essentially its population share and is nonetheless the one state against which the Union's statutory fund-stopping power has been used. Setting Tamil Nadu against Bihar frames the devolution question as rich-against-poor, the framing on which Tamil Nadu loses; setting it against West Bengal isolates the formula. Separating the devolution dispute from the conditionality dispute is the load-bearing analytical move of this phase and these two series are how it is measured.

title: Funds transferred by the Government of India directly to State Implementing Agencies in Tamil Nadu, outside the State Budget

source.name: CAG, State Finances Audit Report No. 2 of 2025, Government of Tamil Nadu, year ended March 2024, Chapter IV para 4.3, Exhibit 4.1 and Table 4.2 (pp. 114-116); back years from the FY2019-20 and FY2022-23 editions. The auditor takes the quantum from the Public Financial Management System of the Controller General of Accounts and sets it against the State Finance Accounts.

Carried as the control: it establishes that release below allocation is the ordinary condition of this scheme in every state, and that a release of zero is therefore a different kind of event rather than the extreme of a continuum.

title: Tax devolution to states as the Union budgeted it, at the start of each year
unit: ₹ crore, current prices, the Union's Budget Estimate of tax devolution as originally presented

source.name: Union Budget, Budget at a Glance, Receipts page, line "Less - State's share" / "Less - States' share", read in each year's own budget as originally presented, across eleven editions. The page is bag2.pdf for FY2014-15 to FY2016-17, bag5.pdf from FY2017-18, and sits inside Budget_at_Glance/budget_at_a_glance.pdf for FY2019-20 to FY2021-22. notes: Authored so that devolution-be-to-actual-gap can be checked by a reader rather than taken on trust: this series and devolution-actual-receipt-budget are its two inputs, and (Actual - BE) divided by BE reproduces all eleven stated values to the stated decimal. Three of the eleven years had two budgets, an interim and a full, with different Budget Estimates; the gap series uses the FULL budget in all three, and that is pinned by arithmetic rather than assumed — substituting the interim estimate breaks all three years and none of the other eight.
caveat: This is what the Union budgeted, not what any Finance Commission recommended and not what the states were entitled to. A state budgets against this number; it is a forecast of gross tax revenue multiplied by a fixed share, and in FY2019-20 and FY2020-21 the forecast was wrong by a fifth and a quarter.

notes: This is the second of the two inputs to devolution-be-to-actual-gap and it is NOT the same instrument as fc-devolution-rupees, which carries Finance Commission Annexure 7.1 figures. Six of the eleven years agree within 240 crore; four do not, and one of those four differs by 67,819 crore. Both instruments are correctly sourced and this drop holds both rather than reconciling them, because no published bridge exists. See P-117.
caveat: An "Actual" here is not final. The Union's own Receipt Budget distinguishes "the amount devolved as per Actuals" from the C&AG-certified actuals, states that the figures "are provisional and may change", and recovers over-devolution from the states in a later year. A gap series computed on this column shows a positive gap as money the states received above budget and cannot show it later being clawed back.
